candidate_relations.reason: The long-RP narrow-complex tachycardia has short retrograde P waves and no documented accessory pathway, so AVRT is a mechanistically different reentrant tachycardia from atypical AVNRT.
Superiorly directed short P waves during a regular long-RP tachycardia can mimic focal atrial tachycardia, but the referenced diagnosis assigns AV-nodal reentry rather than an atrial focus.
A sudden regular narrow-complex rhythm at 170 beats/min with inverted inferior P waves and long RP intervals is not the gradual sinus-rate response expected from deconditioning.
No pulmonary-embolism test or right-heart strain is reported, and the ECG pattern is interpreted as atypical AV-nodal reentry rather than a pulmonary-embolism-triggered atrial focus.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: atrial tachycardia with unproven PE cause

case_quality_flags: electrophysiology confirmation of the reentry mechanism is not included
